subject: Finvere bake-off: sprint commitments, open gaps, and proposed test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@finvere.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Finvere bake-off: sprint commitments, open gaps, and proposed test plan

Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap & proposed next steps so we all stay aligned. I captured what we heard from your team and what Redwood will commit to for the bake-off sprint.

Top pain points (from your call):
- Token cost unpredictability across high-volume batch jobs (peak trading windows).
- P95 latency spikes on longer contexts (>1k tokens) hurting real-time workflows.
- Data residency + auditability requirements for regulatory reporting.

Goals you called out:
- Maintain P95 < 120ms for 512-token response on standard prompt set.
- Reduce per-token inference cost versus current baseline by 20% (at comparable quality).
- Validate audit/logging for retained prompts and KV-cache behavior for compliance.

Decision criteria (what you said matters most):
1) Latency SLOs (P50/P95/P99) under realistic load.
2) Cost per 1M tokens at projected volumes.
3) Security/compliance artifacts (SOC 2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration).
4) Quality parity on answer extraction and entity extraction tasks (no significant degradation).

Open questions we need to resolve before the test window:
- What does your production prompt mix look like (ratio short:long context)? Please use the attached MAP template to capture distributions.
- Any specific vendor features that we should emulate in the micro-tests (e.g., streaming truncation behavior, function-calling contracts)?
- Does Finvere require private deployment (VPC/on-prem) proof-of-concept or is a dedicated-hosted lane acceptable for this phase?

Proposed bake-off micro-test plan (week of Dec 7):
- Day 1: Baseline ingestion & cold-start latency tests (512/1k/2k prompts) — run both single-stream and batch patterns.
- Day 2: Throughput stress (sustained qps for 90m) capturing P50/P95/P99 and token unit cost.
- Day 3: Functional quality tests using your sample prompt set + internal evaluation harness (exact metrics: F1/EM for extraction tasks).
- Day 4: Security/compliance walkthrough and audit log sampling.

Owners & asks:
- Finvere: complete the finvere-map-template.xlsx with prompt distribution and share sample prompts by Dec 3.
- Redwood (Marissa): provide the redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx with test definitions and scoring rubric (attached).
- Redwood (Sean): provide microtest-promptset.jsonl and schedule the test harness run window.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx (test matrix), finvere-map-template.xlsx (prompt distribution template).

If this looks right, can we lock in week-of-Dec-7 for the micro-tests? We can do the test window earlier if you prefer — suggest negotiating schedules this week.

Thanks — looking forward to a productive run.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 17:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Finvere bake-off: sprint commitments, open gaps, and proposed test plan

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the thorough recap — this matches our internal read. A few clarifications and items from our side:

Clarifications:
- Prompt mix: about 60% short (<128 tokens), 30% mid (128–1024), 10% long (>1024). I will fill the template and send by Tue (Dec 1).
- Deployment lane: For this phase we need Redwood to run in Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) so we get deterministic capacity and can evaluate scaling characteristics; we will decide later on Private deployment.

New asks / tests to include:
- KV-cache consistency under burst traffic: we want to ensure cached prefixes don't regress quality for session-based recall. Please add a cache-hit/cold-run comparison in your matrix.
- Audit log sample: we need a sample audit log record format (showing request/response metadata and key IDs) for legal review.

Security docs: please send SOC 2 summary + KMS integration diagram. If you can attach a one-page blurb now that would be helpful; otherwise we will wait for the full package.

Timing: week-of-Dec-7 works for us; Rajiv (cc'd) will coordinate exact test windows with Sean.

Also — are you able to sign our NDA quickly? I can route a DocuSign if that speeds things up.

Thanks,
Ellen
VP, AI Platform, Finvere
ellen.park@finvere.com
+1 (212) 555-7789
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@finvere.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@finvere.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Finvere bake-off: sprint commitments, open gaps, and proposed test plan

Thanks Ellen — quick technical notes and proposed additions to the matrix (so we can be precise in scoring):

1) KV-cache tests: we'll run paired runs with identical session histories and report token-level diff metrics and a session-recall score (simple F1 on entities pulled from memory). That will show whether caching changes generation fidelity.

2) Cold-start / warm-start: We'll include a 30-minute cold-start window and then a warm sustained run to capture step-change behavior.

3) Workload generator: please confirm whether your traffic shape has diurnal spikes (we need to replicate the 15-minute high-volatility windows you referenced). If so, share sample qps curve or we will model a worst-case 3x spike.

I attached microtest-promptset.jsonl — it's a small set we will run initially to sanity-check scoring. We will expand it with your real prompts after you send the MAP template.

Deliverables from Redwood during/after the run:
- Raw latency traces + aggregated P50/P95/P99 per prompt class.
- Token accounting and per-run cost estimates (we'll provide the calculator sheet).
- Sample audit log snippets (sanitized) + SOC2 summary.

I'll let Rajiv and Finvere pick a 3-hour window on Dec 8–9 or Dec 10–11 and Sean/Aditya will stand up the harness and monitor.

Cheers,
Sean
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Finvere bake-off: sprint commitments, open gaps, and proposed test plan

Marissa / Sean —

All good from our side. Rajiv and I reviewed the matrix and the test harness sample prompts — we're comfortable with the scope. Confirming:

- Finvere will provide the MAP template with prompt distribution and 50 representative prompts by Tue, Dec 1 EOD.
- We prefer the Dec 9 window (09:00–12:00 PT) for the micro-tests; Rajiv will send a calendar invite.
- Rajiv requested SOC 2 summary + KMS integration diagram by Mon (Dec 6).
- We'll need a short NDA signed before Redwood ingests any production prompts; please send the DocuSign link.

Marissa — once you send the DocuSign link I can route it internally. Once the NDA is in place we'll share the sample prompts.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Best,
Ellen
